text(await tools.send_message({to:"/root/implement_16", message:"Review current tree: typecheck/lint/tests/build all pass. Main remaining behavior/accessibility risks: (1) delete confirmation is an inline `<section role=\"alertdialog\" aria-modal=\"true\">` with no focus trap and no focus restoration to Delete sighting after Keep sighting; focus is left on an unmounted button/body, contrary to issue's keyboard/focus-safe criterion. Either implement dialog focus management (trap + restore trigger) or don't claim modal semantics. (2) CorrectionEditor catches `onSaved`/`onDeleted` navigation promises? `onSaved(result.sighting)` is not awaited (typed void), so a rejected navigate can become unhandled; same existing callback contract affects route failure visibility. Consider async callback types/await + route-level handling. (3) Current route tests are component callback tests; acceptance asks route tests covering both entry points/navigation visibility, so no regression coverage for actual `from=completion` return query or recent route navigation. New onNotFoundReturn currently deliberately returns capture even from completion; verify this matches intended origin semantics. Otherwise server ordering/contracts look correct; all local checks pass."}));

content.text:
Review complete. `bun run typecheck`, lint, tests, and production build pass.

Findings:

1. The delete confirmation is marked `role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"` but has no focus trap or focus restoration. After “Keep sighting,” focus lands on the unmounted button/body. Implement modal focus management or remove modal semantics.

2. `onSaved`/`onDeleted` callbacks are typed as returning `void`, while route handlers are async navigation calls. Their promises are not awaited, so navigation rejection could become unhandled and provide no visible failure path. Consider async callback types and explicit handling.

3. Tests exercise injected component callbacks, but not actual route navigation. Add coverage for both entry points, `from=completion` return behavior, and navigation visibility as required by issue #16.
